seoTitle: How to Whitelist an IP Address in Google Workspace
metaDescription: Learn how to whitelist a trusted IP address for Gmail in the Google Workspace Admin Console so mail from your servers isn't blocked as spam.
intro: If your organization sends automated email from a custom server or third-party app, whitelisting its IP address ensures those messages reach Workspace inboxes without being flagged as spam. This guide covers how to set that up in the Admin Console.

steps.heading: Locate Gmail settings in the Admin Console
steps.body: Sign in as an admin and navigate to the Apps section, then into Gmail's advanced settings.

steps.heading: Access routing and email whitelist options
steps.body: Within Gmail's settings, find the section for email allowlists or advanced routing rules used to trust specific servers.

steps.heading: Add the IP address or range
steps.body: Enter the trusted IP address, or a range if you're whitelisting a block of addresses, under the email whitelist configuration.

steps.heading: Save and apply the changes
steps.body: Confirm the settings are saved so the whitelist takes effect across your organization's Gmail delivery rules.

steps.heading: Test with a sample email
steps.body: Send a test message from the whitelisted server to confirm it arrives without being filtered, and monitor for any delivery issues.

faq.question: Why would I need to whitelist an IP address in Google Workspace?
faq.answer: This is typically needed when a trusted third-party app or custom mail server sends email that's being incorrectly flagged as spam by default filtering.

faq.question: Is whitelisting an IP address a security risk?
faq.answer: It can be if misused, since whitelisted addresses bypass standard spam checks — only whitelist servers and services you fully trust.

faq.question: Can I whitelist a range of IP addresses instead of just one?
faq.answer: Yes, Google Workspace's routing settings support whitelisting IP ranges, which is useful for services that send from multiple servers.

faq.question: How do I verify my IP whitelist changes are working?
faq.answer: Send a test email from the whitelisted address or server and confirm it lands in the inbox rather than being filtered or blocked.
